candidates.exact_span:
The reasonable potential calculation was performed using test results for those parameters (tested
at MQL) that were greater than the MQL. Detection limit values were used for those parameters
reported as non-detect whose values are above the MQL. For RP calculation purpose, averaged
value of data set is utilized in the RP calculations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which reported values count toward RP (MQL floor, substitution of detection limits for qualifying non-detects, arithmetic mean vs other aggregations used elsewhere in the segment) could change whether reasonable potential is found and therefore whether numeric limits are established as applicable.

candidates.exact_span:
The effluent data for delta-BHC were 0.00245 ug/L (5/20/2020), ND <0.002 ug/L (5/26/2021)
and ND <0.002 ug/L (6/2/2021) with a geometric mean of 0.0013481 ug/L. NMWQS does not
have numeric criteria for delta-BHC. EPA has not published recommended human health
criterion for delta-BHC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether any enforceable numeric discharge limit exists for delta-BHC (given explicit absence of NMWQS and EPA human-health criteria) determines whether reported measurements can be compared to a numeric limit or must be classified as non-comparable monitoring.

candidates.exact_span:
EPA proposes additional delta-BHC monitoring in the effluent to be used in the next permit
cycle should there be sufficient toxicological studies at that time to calculate limitations. As a
result, the permittee is required to submit a detailed plan to test for Delta-BHC at the source
water intake within six months after the effective date of the permit to both EPA and NMED for
approval. The plan must also include any use of delta-BHC at the facility, if any. Once approved,
the permittee must collect and analyze samples for delta-BHC at least once a quarter or more
frequent during the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether delta-BHC monitoring was required during Federal FY2025 depends on interpreting the plan-approval gate, the six-month post-effective-date deadline, and whether FY2025 falls within permit years 2–5; different readings change obligation status and how absent results are classified (not yet required vs missing required evidence).

candidates.exact_span: The results of this study shall be attached to the DMR reports to EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether missing delta-BHC entries on DMRs represent inadequate evidence of required monitoring versus an allowed no-data state hinges on interpreting this attachment obligation relative to when the approved study schedule actually begins.
